source.text: מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְאֵיתָ֥ן הָֽאֶזְרָחִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.

en.L: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.
en.B: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.
en.R: A song to teach, by Ethan the Ezrahite.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: maskil: a song of insight, or a skillful song
decisions.reason: As in 88:1; its exact sense is no longer known.

Ethan was a famous wise man (1 Kings 5) and is listed with Heman among the sons of Zerah of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:6). An Ethan was also one of David's chief singers (1 Chronicles 15:19). Psalm 88 is by Heman the Ezrahite.

decisions.choice: a royal psalm on the covenant with David
decisions.reason: The psalm praises God's loyal love and faithfulness (verses 2-19), recalls his promise to David's line (20-38), then laments that the king has been defeated and his crown thrown down (39-52). The promise is the one given through Nathan in 2 Samuel 7.
Readable gives the likely sense of the term (m2).

source.text: חַֽסְדֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עוֹלָ֣ם אָשִׁ֑ירָה לְדֹ֥ר וָדֹ֓ר׀אוֹדִ֖יעַ אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בְּפִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] loyal loves of YHWH forever I will sing; to generation and generation I will make known your faithfulness with my mouth.

en.L: Of the loyal love[s] of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will sing forever; to generation and generation I will make known {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness with my mouth.
en.B: Forever I will sing of the loyal love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown; to one generation after another my mouth will tell how faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.
en.R: I will always sing about the faithful love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will tell people in every generation how faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: loyal loves: God's acts of loyal love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith within a bond (86:5). The plural means the many acts of that love, above all the promises to David; verse 50 asks where these "former acts of loyal love" have gone.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: God can be relied on
decisions.reason: The word ('emunah) is firmness, reliability. With chesed it is the theme of the psalm: each occurs seven times (chesed in verses 2, 3, 15, 25, 29, 34, 50; 'emunah in verses 2, 3, 6, 9, 25, 34, 50).

decisions.choice: your: the psalm turns to address God
decisions.reason: The first line speaks about the LORD; the second speaks to him. Psalms often move between the two.

source.text: כִּֽי־אָמַ֗רְתִּי ע֭וֹלָם חֶ֣סֶד יִבָּנֶ֑ה שָׁמַ֓יִם׀תָּכִ֖ן אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For I have said, "Forever loyal love will be built; [the] heavens — you establish your faithfulness in them."

en.L: For I have said: Loyal love will be built forever; [as for the] heavens, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} establish {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in them.
en.B: For I declare that loyal love is built to last forever; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness firm in the heavens.
en.R: I say that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love will last forever. You have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness as firm as the sky above.

decisions.choice: built: raised up like a house
decisions.reason: God's loyal love is pictured as a building that will stand forever. The same verb is used in verse 5 ("I will build your throne") and in the promise to build David a house (2 Samuel 7:27).
The Hebrew text has "I have said"; the ancient Greek translation has "you have said", which would make verses 3-5 all God's words.
As in verse 2 (chesed, 'emunah).

source.text: כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִבְחִירִ֑י נִ֝שְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי לְדָוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I have cut a covenant with my chosen [one]; I have sworn to David my servant:

en.L: "I have cut a covenant with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen [one]; I have sworn to David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant:
en.B: "With the one I chose I have made a covenant; to David, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, I have given {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oath:
en.R: God said, "I made a covenant with the one I chose. I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word with an oath to David, who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}:

decisions.reason: Verses 4-5 are God's own words, though no words such as "you said" introduce them. They sum up the promise that verses 20-38 give at length.

God's promise through the prophet Nathan, that David's line and throne would last forever (2 Samuel 7:8-16). That passage does not use the word "covenant", but other passages call it so (2 Samuel 23:5; 132:11-12).

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: make a covenant
decisions.reason: Covenants were made with a sacrifice cut in pieces (Genesis 15:9-18), so a covenant is "cut". Literal keeps the idiom.
Readable names the speaker (m1).

source.text: עַד־ע֭וֹלָם אָכִ֣ין זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וּבָנִ֨יתִי לְדֹר־וָד֖וֹר כִּסְאֲךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: "Until forever I will establish your offspring, and I will build to generation and generation your throne." Selah.

en.L: 'Forever I will establish your offspring, and I will build your throne to generation and generation.'" Selah
en.B: 'I will make your line secure forever and make your throne stand for every generation.'" Selah
en.R: 'I will make sure your descendants last forever. Your throne will stand in every generation.'" Selah

decisions.reason: These are the words of 2 Samuel 7:12-16: "I will establish ... your throne will be established forever." Peter refers to this oath in Acts 2:30, of a descendant of David set on his throne.

decisions.choice: your offspring: your line of descendants
decisions.reason: The word (zera') is "seed": the royal line that follows David.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: וְי֘וֹד֤וּ שָׁמַ֣יִם פִּלְאֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה אַף־אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בִּקְהַ֥ל קְדֹשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] heavens praise your wonder, YHWH, also your faithfulness in [the] assembly of [the] holy [ones].

en.L: And the heavens praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonder[s], {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, also {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
en.B: The heavens give thanks for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in the gathering of the holy ones.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the skies praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do. The angels in heaven praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful.

decisions.choice: the holy ones: the heavenly beings around God
decisions.reason: The "holy ones" here are the beings of heaven who serve God, as in verse 8 and Job 5:1; Deuteronomy 33:2-3.
The word (pele') is singular and collective, as in 88:11.

alternatives: the assembly of the holy ones
decisions.reason: Readable names who the holy ones are (m1).

source.text: כִּ֤י מִ֣י בַ֭שַּׁחַק יַעֲרֹ֣ךְ לַיהוָ֑ה יִדְמֶ֥ה לַ֝יהוָ֗ה בִּבְנֵ֥י אֵלִים׃

records.literal_gloss: For who in the skies can compare to YHWH, [who] is like YHWH among [the] sons of gods?

en.L: For who in the skies can be compared to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [who] is like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} among the sons of gods?
en.B: For who in the clouds above is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s equal? Which of the heavenly powers is like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.R: No one in heaven can compare with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. None of the angels is like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.reason: As in 29:1, "sons of 'elim" means beings of the heavenly world, not other gods equal to the LORD. The point is that none of them can compare with him.
The word (shachaq) is the clouds or the sky, here the realm above where these beings are.
Readable names who these beings are (m1).

source.text: אֵ֣ל נַ֭עֲרָץ בְּסוֹד־קְדֹשִׁ֣ים רַבָּ֑ה וְ֝נוֹרָ֗א עַל־כָּל־סְבִיבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: God [is] dreaded in [the] council of [the] holy [ones], greatly, and feared above all [those] around him.

en.L: God [is] dreaded in the council of the holy ones, greatly, and feared above all who [are] around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: God is held in great awe in the court of the holy ones, and feared above all who stand around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: When the holy ones meet around God, they stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is far more awesome than any of them.

decisions.choice: the council of the holy ones: God's heavenly court
decisions.reason: Scripture pictures God as a king surrounded by his court of heavenly beings (82:1; 1 Kings 22:19; Job 1:6).

decisions.choice: greatly: with the first line or the second
alternatives: a great God, awesome above all around him
decisions.reason: The word "great" may belong with "dreaded" (greatly dreaded) or with the council (the great council).

source.text: יְהוָ֤ה׀אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י צְבָא֗וֹת מִֽי־כָֽמ֖וֹךָ חֲסִ֥ין׀יָ֑הּ וֶ֝אֱמֽוּנָתְךָ֗ סְבִיבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH God of hosts, who [is] like you? Mighty [one], Yah, and your faithfulness [is] around you.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, mighty {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}? And {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness [is] all around {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, who is as strong as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}? Your faithfulness surrounds {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on every side.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, no one is as strong as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}. Your faithfulness is all around {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The title (YHWH 'Elohe tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name YHWH, as in "Hallelu-yah" ("Praise Yah").
The word (chasin) is found only here in the Bible; it is related to words for strength.
God's faithfulness surrounds him like a garment or like attendants around a king (verse 15).

source.text: אַתָּ֣ה מ֭וֹשֵׁל בְּגֵא֣וּת הַיָּ֑ם בְּשׂ֥וֹא גַ֝לָּ֗יו אַתָּ֥ה תְשַׁבְּחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You rule over [the] swelling of the sea; when its waves rise, you still them.

en.L: You rule over the swelling of the sea; when its waves rise, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} still them.
en.B: You are master of the proud sea; when its waves rear up, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hush them.
en.R: You control the wild sea. When its waves rise high, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make them calm.

decisions.choice: the sea: the power of chaos that God masters
decisions.reason: In the Psalms the raging sea stands for everything that threatens God's ordered world (65:8; 93:3-4). Jesus' calming of the storm (Mark 4:39) shows the same power.
The word (ge'ut) means rising up, and so pride, as in 46:4.

source.text: אַתָּ֤ה דִכִּ֣אתָ כֶחָלָ֣ל רָ֑הַב בִּזְר֥וֹעַ עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ פִּזַּ֥רְתָּ אוֹיְבֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You crushed like [one] slain Rahab; with [the] arm of your strength you scattered your enemies.

en.L: You crushed Rahab like [one] slain; with the arm of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} scattered {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies.
en.B: You crushed Rahab like one cut down in battle; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} powerful arm sent {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies running.
en.R: You crushed the sea monster Rahab and killed it. With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} scattered {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies.

decisions.choice: Rahab: the sea monster of chaos
decisions.reason: Rahab is a picture of the chaos of the sea that God defeated (Job 26:12; Isaiah 51:9). Isaiah 51:9-10 ties it to the crossing of the sea at the exodus, and 87:4 uses the name for Egypt.

decisions.choice: the arm of your strength: your power in action
decisions.reason: God's arm is his strength at work, as at the exodus (Exodus 6:6).
Readable says who Rahab is (m1).

source.text: לְךָ֣ שָׁ֭מַיִם אַף־לְךָ֥ אָ֑רֶץ תֵּבֵ֥ל וּ֝מְלֹאָ֗הּ אַתָּ֥ה יְסַדְתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: To you [are the] heavens, also to you [the] earth; [the] world and what fills it, you founded them.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [belong the] heavens, also to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [belongs the] earth; the world and what fills it, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} founded them.
en.B: The heavens are {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, and the earth is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} as well; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} laid the foundations of the world and of everything in it.
en.R: Heaven belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and so does the earth. You made the world and everything in it.

decisions.choice: the world and what fills it
decisions.reason: As in 24:1-2: the world belongs to God because he founded it.

decisions.choice: creation shows God's right to rule
decisions.reason: Verses 10-15 praise God as creator and king; the same God made the promise to David's line.

source.text: צָפ֣וֹן וְ֭יָמִין אַתָּ֣ה בְרָאתָ֑ם תָּב֥וֹר וְ֝חֶרְמ֗וֹן בְּשִׁמְךָ֥ יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: North and south, you created them; Tabor and Hermon at your name shout for joy.

en.L: North and south, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} created them; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.
en.B: North and south are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} creation; Tabor and Hermon ring with joy at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.
en.R: You made the north and the south. The mountains Tabor and Hermon shout for joy to praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: Tabor and Hermon: mountains of the north
decisions.reason: Mount Tabor rises alone in the plain of Galilee; Mount Hermon, the highest mountain of the land, stands on its northern border. Even the great mountains praise their maker.
The words name the directions, so the line takes in all the world. "North" (tsafon) is also the name of a mountain (48:3), and some read both words as mountains beside Tabor and Hermon.
Readable says what rejoicing at God's name means.

source.text: לְךָ֣ זְ֭רוֹעַ עִם־גְּבוּרָ֑ה תָּעֹ֥ז יָ֝דְךָ֗ תָּר֥וּם יְמִינֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: To you [is] an arm with might; strong [is] your hand, high [is] your right hand.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [belongs] an arm with might; strong [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, high [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand.
en.B: Yours is an arm full of might; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand has strength, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand is lifted high.
en.R: Your arm is mighty. Your hand is strong. Your right hand is raised high to win.

decisions.choice: your right hand is high: raised in victory
decisions.reason: A raised right hand is power ready to strike and victory won (118:16). Verse 43 says God has raised the right hand of the king's enemies instead.
Readable makes the sense of the raised hand explicit (m1).

source.text: צֶ֣דֶק וּ֭מִשְׁפָּט מְכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֶ֑ךָ חֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת יְֽקַדְּמ֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Righteousness and justice [are the] foundation of your throne; loyal love and truth go before your face.

en.L: Righteousness and justice [are the] foundation of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne; loyal love and truth go before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face.
en.B: Your throne rests on what is right and just; loyal love and faithfulness walk ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: You rule with fairness and justice. Your faithful love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth go out ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The same words are in 97:2. God's rule rests on doing right; it is the model for David's throne (72:1-2).

decisions.choice: go before your face: walk ahead like attendants
decisions.reason: Loyal love and truth are pictured as servants going ahead of a king. The verb (qiddem) is the one used in 88:14.
The pair chesed and 'emet, as in Exodus 34:6 (86:15).

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם יוֹדְעֵ֣י תְרוּעָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה בְּֽאוֹר־פָּנֶ֥יךָ יְהַלֵּכֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is] the people knowing [the] joyful shout; YHWH, in [the] light of your face they walk.

en.L: How blessed [is] the people who know the joyful shout; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, they walk in the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face.
en.B: How blessed are the people who have learned to shout for joy in worship; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, they live in the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.
en.R: Life is truly good for people who know how to shout praises to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, they live in the warm light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor.

decisions.reason: As in 1:1 ('ashre): a life that is good because it is right with God.

decisions.choice: the joyful shout: the shout of worship at the festivals
decisions.reason: The word (teru'ah) is the loud shout or trumpet blast that hails a king and fills the festivals (47:6; Numbers 23:21).

decisions.choice: the light of your face: your favor
decisions.reason: God's face shining on someone is his favor and blessing (4:7; Numbers 6:25).

source.text: בְּ֭שִׁמְךָ יְגִיל֣וּן כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וּבְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ יָרֽוּמוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: In your name they rejoice all the day, and in your righteousness they are exalted.

en.L: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name they rejoice all the day, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness they are lifted up.
en.B: They find joy in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name the whole day, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness raises them up.
en.R: They are glad all day long because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do what is right, they can hold their heads high.

decisions.choice: your name: God as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: As in 86:11.
As in 88:13: God doing right by his people lifts them up.

decisions.choice: because of you; because you do what is right, they can hold their heads high
alternatives: in your name; in your righteousness they are exalted
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrases mean (m1, m2).

source.text: כִּֽי־תִפְאֶ֣רֶת עֻזָּ֣מוֹ אָ֑תָּה וּ֝בִרְצֹנְךָ֗ תָּר֥וּם קַרְנֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] glory of their strength [are] you, and in your favor our horn is exalted.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] the glory of their strength, and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor our horn is lifted high.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the splendor of their strength, and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodwill our strength is raised high.
en.R: You are their strength and their glory. Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are kind to us, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us strong.

decisions.choice: is exalted: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes "you exalt" and its notes say to read "is exalted". The meaning is the same: God's favor makes them strong.
A raised horn is the strength of a wild ox, a picture of power and victory (75:5; 92:11; 1 Samuel 2:1).

decisions.choice: their, our: the people of verse 16
decisions.reason: "Their" is the people who know the joyful shout; the psalmist then joins them with "our".

decisions.choice: our strength (B); you make us strong (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the horn stands for (m2); Literal keeps it.

source.text: כִּ֣י לַֽ֭יהוָה מָֽגִנֵּ֑נוּ וְלִקְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מַלְכֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For to YHWH [belongs] our shield, and to [the] Holy One of Israel our king.

en.L: For to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs] our shield, and to the Holy One of Israel our king.
en.B: For the shield that protects us is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s, and the king who rules us belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
en.R: Our king, who protects us like a shield, belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the holy God of Israel.

alternatives: the LORD is our shield, and the Holy One of Israel is our king
decisions.reason: "Our shield" and "our king" stand in parallel, so the shield is the king who protects his people (84:10 "our shield ... your anointed"). The king belongs to God, which leads into the promise of verses 20-38. The words can also be read "the LORD is our shield, the Holy One of Israel our king".
A title for God used often in Isaiah (Isaiah 1:4) and in 71:22 and 78:41.
Readable says plainly who the Holy One is (m2).

source.text: אָ֤ז דִּבַּ֥רְתָּֽ־בְחָ֡זוֹן לַֽחֲסִידֶ֗יךָ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁוִּ֣יתִי עֵ֭זֶר עַל־גִּבּ֑וֹר הֲרִימ֖וֹתִי בָח֣וּר מֵעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Then you spoke in a vision to your faithful [ones] and said, "I have set help on a mighty [one]; I have exalted a chosen [one] from [the] people.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke in a vision to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful ones, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, "I have set help on a mighty [one]; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
en.B: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke in a vision to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal ones and said, "I have laid help on a mighty man; I have lifted high a man I chose from the people.
en.R: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke in a vision to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful people. You said, "I have given strength to a mighty warrior. I have chosen a man from among the people and made him great.

decisions.choice: a vision to your faithful ones: the word through Nathan
alternatives: to your faithful one (some Hebrew manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The promise came to David through the prophet Nathan in a vision at night (2 Samuel 7:4-17). Some Hebrew manuscripts have the singular, "your faithful one".
From here to the end of verse 38 God himself speaks, so the quotation opens here and closes at verse 38.

decisions.choice: a chosen one: one God picked out
decisions.reason: The word (bachur) means "chosen" and is also used for a young man in his prime. Both fit David, chosen from among the people as a youth (1 Samuel 16:1-13).

source.text: מָ֭צָאתִי דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֑י בְּשֶׁ֖מֶן קָדְשִׁ֣י מְשַׁחְתִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him,

en.L: I have found David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy oil I have anointed him,
en.B: I found David, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; I have poured {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy oil on him to make him king,
en.R: I found David, who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I poured {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy oil on him to make him king.

decisions.reason: Paul quotes these words in Acts 13:22, joined with 1 Samuel 13:14: "I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my heart."
Samuel poured oil on David's head to mark him as God's chosen king (1 Samuel 16:13). "Anointed" (mashiach) is the word behind "Messiah".
Balanced and Readable say what anointing meant here (m2).
The sentence continues into verse 22 ("with whom my hand ..."), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָ֭דִי תִּכּ֣וֹן עִמּ֑וֹ אַף־זְרוֹעִ֥י תְאַמְּצֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: with whom my hand will be steadfast; also my arm will strengthen him.

en.L: with whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand will be steadfast; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm also will strengthen him.
en.B: and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand will stay with him, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm will make him strong.
en.R: My hand will always be with him to help him. My arm will make him strong.

decisions.choice: my hand, my arm: my power at work for him
decisions.reason: God's hand and arm are his strength in action (verses 11, 14), now given to the king.

source.text: לֹֽא־יַשִּׁ֣א אוֹיֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וּבֶן־עַ֝וְלָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will deceive an enemy him, and a son of injustice not will afflict him.

en.L: An enemy will not deceive him, and {{gender:a child of injustice|a son of injustice}} will not afflict him.
en.B: No enemy will outwit him, and no one who does wrong will bring him low.
en.R: His enemies will not trick him. Evil people will not crush him.

decisions.choice: deceive: get the better of him
decisions.reason: The verb (nasha') may mean "deceive" or, from a similar root, "press as a creditor". Either way, no enemy will gain the advantage over him.

decisions.choice: the son of injustice will not afflict him
decisions.reason: The words echo 2 Samuel 7:10: "sons of injustice will no longer afflict them". A "son of injustice" is someone marked by wrongdoing.

source.text: וְכַתּוֹתִ֣י מִפָּנָ֣יו צָרָ֑יו וּמְשַׂנְאָ֥יו אֶגּֽוֹף׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will crush from before him his foes, and those hating him I will strike.

en.L: And I will crush his foes before him, and those who hate him I will strike down.
en.B: I will shatter his foes before his eyes and cut down the people who hate him.
en.R: I will crush his enemies as he faces them. I will strike down everyone who hates him.

decisions.reason: As God told David, "I have cut off all your enemies from before you" (2 Samuel 7:9). Verses 41-44 lament that the opposite has happened.

source.text: וֶֽאֶֽמוּנָתִ֣י וְחַסְדִּ֣י עִמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בִשְׁמִ֗י תָּר֥וּם קַרְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And my faithfulness and my loyal love [will be] with him, and in my name will be exalted his horn.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithfulness and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love [will be] with him, and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name his horn will be lifted high.
en.B: My faithfulness and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love will stay beside him, and through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name his strength will rise.
en.R: I will be faithful to him and always love him. Through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power he will grow strong.

decisions.reason: The two theme words of the psalm (verse 2), now promised to the king.

decisions.choice: his horn will be exalted: he will be strong and victorious
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

decisions.choice: in my name: by who I am and the power I have
decisions.reason: God's name is himself as he has made himself known (verse 17). The king's strength will come from God.

decisions.choice: his strength (B); he will grow strong (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י בַיָּ֣ם יָד֑וֹ וּֽבַנְּהָר֥וֹת יְמִינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will set on the sea his hand, and on the rivers his right hand.

en.L: And I will set his hand on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers.
en.B: I will put the sea under his hand and the rivers under his right hand.
en.R: I will let him rule all the way to the sea and to the great rivers.

decisions.choice: the sea and the rivers: the limits of his rule
decisions.reason: The sea and the River (the Euphrates) mark the bounds of the promised land (Exodus 23:31; 72:8). The king is given a share in God's rule over the sea (verse 10).
Readable says what setting his hand on them means (m1).

source.text: ה֣וּא יִ֭קְרָאֵנִי אָ֣בִי אָ֑תָּה אֵ֝לִ֗י וְצ֣וּר יְשׁוּעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: He will call me, 'My father [are] you, my God and [the] rock of my salvation.'

en.L: He will call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'My Father [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God, and the rock of my salvation.'
en.B: He will call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'It is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who are my Father, my God, my rock where I am safe.'
en.R: He will pray to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'My Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my God. You are the rock who keeps me safe.'

decisions.choice: my Father: the king as God's son
decisions.reason: God promised of David's son, "I will be his father, and he will be a son to me" (2 Samuel 7:14; see 2:7). The king is God's son by adoption and covenant. The New Testament applies 2 Samuel 7:14 to Jesus (Hebrews 1:5).

decisions.choice: rock of my salvation: the God who keeps me safe
decisions.reason: A rock is a place of refuge high above danger (18:3; 95:1).

decisions.choice: the king speaks as a man
decisions.reason: In this psalm the king is a human king; God's pronouns are marked but the king's are not.

source.text: אַף־אָ֭נִי בְּכ֣וֹר אֶתְּנֵ֑הוּ עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן לְמַלְכֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also I firstborn will make him, highest of [the] kings of [the] earth.

en.L: Also I will make him [the] firstborn, highest of the kings of the earth.
en.B: And I will give him the rank of firstborn, set high above every king on earth.
en.R: I will treat him as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} firstborn son, the greatest of all the kings on earth.

decisions.choice: firstborn: the son with the first rank and the inheritance
decisions.reason: The firstborn son held first place in the family and a double share (Deuteronomy 21:17). God called Israel "my firstborn son" (Exodus 4:22); here the king receives that rank.

decisions.choice: highest: the word used of God as "Most High"
decisions.reason: The word ('elyon) is the title of God in 87:5. The king is set as high among earthly kings as God is above all.
Revelation 1:5 calls Jesus "the firstborn of the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth", in words that echo this verse.
Readable says whose firstborn (m1).

source.text: לְ֭עוֹלָ֗ם אֶשְׁמָר־ל֣וֹ חַסְדִּ֑י וּ֝בְרִיתִ֗י נֶאֱמֶ֥נֶת לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Forever I will keep for him my loyal love, and my covenant [will be] firm for him.

en.L: Forever I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love for him, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant [will] stand firm for him.
en.B: I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love for him forever, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with him will hold fast.
en.R: I will always love him faithfully. My covenant with him will never be broken.

decisions.choice: I will keep: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes the verb in one form and its notes say to read it in another. The meaning is the same.
As in verse 2 (chesed).
The verb (ne'eman) comes from the same root as 'emunah, "faithfulness".

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י לָעַ֣ד זַרְע֑וֹ וְ֝כִסְא֗וֹ כִּימֵ֥י שָׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will set forever his offspring, and his throne as [the] days of [the] heavens.

en.L: And I will set his offspring forever, and his throne as the days of [the] heavens.
en.B: I will make his line last for all time, and his throne as long as the sky endures.
en.R: His family line will never end. His kingdom will last as long as the sky above.

decisions.choice: as the days of the heavens: as long as the sky lasts
decisions.reason: A way of saying "forever" (Deuteronomy 11:21).
As in verse 5.

source.text: אִם־יַֽעַזְב֣וּ בָ֭נָיו תּוֹרָתִ֑י וּ֝בְמִשְׁפָּטַ֗י לֹ֣א יֵלֵכֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: If his sons forsake my instruction and in my judgments not walk,

en.L: If his sons forsake {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and do not walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments,
en.B: If his descendants abandon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and do not live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings,
en.R: But suppose his descendants turn away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and do not obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws.

decisions.reason: Verses 31-34 take up 2 Samuel 7:14-15: when David's son does wrong, God will discipline him, but his loyal love will not be taken away.
The word (torah) is instruction, God's teaching for life (1:2).
The "if" clauses of verses 31-32 lead to "then" in verse 33, so verses 31 and 32 end with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
"Sons" here are the kings of David's line after him.

source.text: אִם־חֻקֹּתַ֥י יְחַלֵּ֑לוּ וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁמֹֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: if my statutes they profane and my commandments not keep,

en.L: if they profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments,
en.B: if they treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} decrees as nothing and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands,
en.R: Suppose they break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules and do not do what I command.

decisions.reason: The verb (chillel) is to treat what is holy as ordinary. It comes again in verse 35 ("I will not profane my covenant") and verse 40 ("you have profaned his crown").

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י בְשֵׁ֣בֶט פִּשְׁעָ֑ם וּבִנְגָעִ֥ים עֲוֺנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: then I will punish with a rod their transgression and with blows their iniquity.

en.L: then I will punish their transgression with a rod and their iniquity with blows.
en.B: then I will call their rebellion to account with the rod and their guilt with beatings.
en.R: Then I will punish them for their sin and wrongdoing, as a father disciplines his children with a rod.

decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will discipline him with the rod of men". The punishment is that of a father, not the end of the covenant (verse 34).
The verb (paqad) is "visit"; with sin it means to deal with it, to punish.

decisions.choice: as a father disciplines his children
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the rod from 2 Samuel 7:14 (m1).

source.text: וְ֭חַסְדִּי לֹֽא־אָפִ֣יר מֵֽעִמּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־אֲ֝שַׁקֵּ֗ר בֶּאֱמוּנָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But my loyal love not I will break off from him, and not I will be false to my faithfulness.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love I will not break off from him, and I will not be false to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithfulness.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love I will never cut off from him, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithfulness will not prove false.
en.R: But I will never stop loving him with faithful love. I will always keep faith with him.

decisions.choice: my loyal love will not depart
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:15: "my loyal love will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul".
As in verse 2. These two words are what verse 50 will ask about.

source.text: לֹא־אֲחַלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתִ֑י וּמוֹצָ֥א שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י לֹ֣א אֲשַׁנֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not I will profane my covenant, and [the] going out of my lips not I will change.

en.L: I will not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, and what has gone out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} lips I will not change.
en.B: I will never desecrate {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant; what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} lips have spoken I will not change.
en.R: I will not break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant. I will not take back anything I have said.

decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 32: the kings may profane God's statutes, but God will not profane his covenant.

decisions.choice: what has gone out of my lips: what I have said
decisions.reason: A promise spoken is a word that has gone out of the mouth and cannot be called back (Isaiah 55:11).

source.text: אַ֭חַת נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי בְקָדְשִׁ֑י אִֽם־לְדָוִ֥ד אֲכַזֵּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Once I have sworn by my holiness: if to David I lie!

en.L: Once I have sworn by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness: I will not lie to David.
en.B: I have sworn by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness, once and for all, that I will never lie to David:
en.R: I have made a solemn promise, swearing by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own holiness. I will never lie to David.

decisions.choice: if I lie: an oath that I will not lie
decisions.reason: An oath in the form "if I do this ..." leaves the curse unspoken; it is a strong "I will never".

decisions.choice: sworn by my holiness: by God's own being
decisions.reason: God has nothing greater to swear by than himself (Amos 4:2; Hebrews 6:13).

source.text: זַ֭רְעוֹ לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִהְיֶ֑ה וְכִסְא֖וֹ כַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ נֶגְדִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: His offspring forever will be, and his throne like the sun before me,

en.L: His offspring will be forever, and his throne like the sun before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.B: his line will last forever, and his throne will stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like the sun,
en.R: His family line will last forever. His kingdom will last before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as long as the sun.

decisions.choice: like the sun and the moon
decisions.reason: Compare 72:5, 17 and Jeremiah 33:20-21: God's covenant with David is as sure as the order of day and night.
The sentence continues into verse 38, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: כְּ֭יָרֵחַ יִכּ֣וֹן עוֹלָ֑ם וְעֵ֥ד בַּ֝שַּׁ֗חַק נֶאֱמָ֥ן סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: like [the] moon it will be established forever, and a witness in the sky [is] faithful." Selah.

en.L: like the moon it will be established forever, and the witness in the sky [is] faithful." Selah
en.B: it will be made firm forever like the moon, that faithful witness in the clouds." Selah
en.R: It will last forever, like the moon. The moon in the sky is a faithful witness to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise." Selah

alternatives: the witness in the sky (God himself) is faithful
decisions.reason: The faithful witness is probably the moon, which keeps its course as a sign that the covenant stands. It may also be God himself, witness to his own oath.
The speech that began in verse 20 ends with this verse.
Readable says what the moon witnesses to (m1).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתִּמְאָ֑ס הִ֝תְעַבַּ֗רְתָּ עִם־מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: But you have spurned and rejected; you have been furious with your anointed.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have cast off and rejected; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been furious with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed.
en.B: But now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have thrown him off and rejected him; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are enraged with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed king.
en.R: But now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen king and rejected him. You are very angry with him.

decisions.choice: but you: the turn from promise to lament
decisions.reason: After God's oath (verses 20-38) the psalm turns sharply: what has happened to the king seems to deny the promise. Verses 39-52 set the oath against the defeat and ask God to remember.

decisions.choice: your anointed: the king of David's line
decisions.reason: The anointed (mashiach) is the king anointed with oil (verse 21; 2:2). The word lies behind "Messiah" and "Christ".
As in 88:15 (zanach).
The Hebrew verbs have no object; "your anointed" at the end of the line is the one rejected.

source.text: נֵ֭אַרְתָּה בְּרִ֣ית עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ חִלַּ֖לְתָּ לָאָ֣רֶץ נִזְרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: You have renounced [the] covenant of your servant; you have profaned to the ground his crown.

en.L: You have renounced the covenant of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have profaned his crown to the ground.
en.B: You have disowned the covenant with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have thrown his crown in the dirt and defiled it.
en.R: You have turned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} back on the covenant {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. You have thrown his crown in the dirt.

decisions.reason: The verb (na'ar) is rare; Lamentations 2:7 uses it for God disowning his sanctuary.

decisions.choice: profaned: the word of verses 32 and 35
decisions.reason: God said he would not profane his covenant (verse 35); now it seems he has profaned the king's crown.

source.text: פָּרַ֥צְתָּ כָל־גְּדֵרֹתָ֑יו שַׂ֖מְתָּ מִבְצָרָ֣יו מְחִתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have broken through all his walls; you have made his strongholds a ruin.

en.L: You have broken through all his walls; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made his strongholds a ruin.
en.B: You have torn gaps in all his walls and left his fortresses in rubble.
en.R: You have knocked down the walls around him. You have turned his forts into ruins.

decisions.choice: his walls, his strongholds: the defenses of his kingdom
decisions.reason: The king is pictured as a city or a vineyard whose walls are broken, open to anyone (80:13).

source.text: שַׁ֭סֻּהוּ כָּל־עֹ֣בְרֵי דָ֑רֶךְ הָיָ֥ה חֶ֝רְפָּ֗ה לִשְׁכֵנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: They have plundered him, all passing by [the] road; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.

en.L: All who pass by on the road have plundered him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.
en.B: Everyone who comes along the road has robbed him; his neighbors treat him with scorn.
en.R: Everyone who walks by takes what they want from him. The nations around him laugh at him.

decisions.reason: The surrounding peoples mock Israel's defeat (44:14; 79:4).
Readable says who the neighbors are (m1).

source.text: הֲ֭רִימוֹתָ יְמִ֣ין צָרָ֑יו הִ֝שְׂמַ֗חְתָּ כָּל־אוֹיְבָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: You have exalted [the] right hand of his foes; you have made rejoice all his enemies.

en.L: You have raised high the right hand of his foes; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made all his enemies rejoice.
en.B: You have made his foes' right hand strong and filled all his enemies with joy.
en.R: You have let his enemies win. You have made them all happy.

decisions.choice: raised the right hand: given victory
decisions.reason: God's own right hand is "high" (verse 14) and he promised to strengthen the king (verses 22, 26); now he has raised the enemies' hand instead.

alternatives: raised the right hand of his foes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

source.text: אַף־תָּ֭שִׁיב צ֣וּר חַרְבּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א הֲ֝קֵימֹת֗וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Also you turn back [the] edge of his sword, and not you have made him stand in the battle.

en.L: Yes, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn back the edge of his sword, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not made him stand in the battle.
en.B: Yes, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have blunted his sword's edge and left him unable to stand in the fight.
en.R: You have made his sword useless, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not helped him win his battles.

decisions.reason: The word (tsur) is usually "rock"; here, as with knives of flint (Joshua 5:2), it is the sharp edge of the sword.

decisions.choice: not made him stand: not upheld him
decisions.reason: To stand in battle is to hold one's ground; God has let the king fall.

source.text: הִשְׁבַּ֥תָּ מִטְּהָר֑וֹ וְ֝כִסְא֗וֹ לָאָ֥רֶץ מִגַּֽרְתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have made cease from his splendor, and his throne to the ground you have hurled.

en.L: You have made [him] cease from his splendor, and his throne {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have hurled to the ground.
en.B: You have made his glory fade and thrown his throne down into the dust.
en.R: You have taken away his glory. You have knocked his throne to the ground.

decisions.choice: his splendor: his brightness, his royal glory
decisions.reason: The Hebrew form is unusual and seems to mean "from his brightness". Some suggest a slightly different text, "the scepter from his hand". The sense is that his royal glory is gone.

source.text: הִ֭קְצַרְתָּ יְמֵ֣י עֲלוּמָ֑יו הֶֽעֱטִ֨יתָ עָלָ֖יו בּוּשָׁ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have cut short [the] days of his youth; you have wrapped on him shame. Selah.

en.L: You have cut short the days of his youth; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have wrapped him in shame. Selah
en.B: You have made his young days short and covered him with disgrace like a cloak. Selah
en.R: You have cut his young years short. You have dressed him in shame. Selah

decisions.choice: the days of his youth cut short
decisions.reason: The king's strength has ended early: he has grown old before his time, or his reign has been cut off while he was young.
Shame is pictured as clothing wrapped around him, in place of royal robes (109:29).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: עַד־מָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּסָּתֵ֣ר לָנֶ֑צַח תִּבְעַ֖ר כְּמוֹ־אֵ֣שׁ חֲמָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when, YHWH, will you hide yourself forever? Will burn like fire your wrath?

en.L: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} forever? Will {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath burn like fire?
en.B: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} hidden forever? Will {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger go on burning like fire?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how long will this go on? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stay hidden forever? Will {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger keep burning like a fire?

decisions.reason: Psalm 79:5 asks almost the same: "How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?"

decisions.choice: hide yourself: stay away and not help
decisions.reason: As in 88:15 and 13:2: God's hiding is his absence when he is needed.

source.text: זְכָר־אֲנִ֥י מֶה־חָ֑לֶד עַל־מַה־שָּׁ֝֗וְא בָּרָ֥אתָ כָל־בְּנֵי־אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember I, what [is my] lifespan! For what emptiness have you created all [the] children of humankind?

en.L: Remember, I, what [my] lifespan [is]! For what emptiness have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} created all the children of {{gender:humankind|man}}?
en.B: Remember how brief my life is! Is it for nothing that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have created every human being?
en.R: Remember how short my life is! Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made all people for no purpose at all?

decisions.choice: remember, I: remember me and how short my life is
alternatives: remember, Lord, what my lifespan is
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is abrupt: "remember, I, what is lifespan". It asks God to remember the speaker and how short his life is. Some read "Lord" for "I", as in verse 51.

decisions.choice: lifespan: the short span of life
decisions.reason: The word (cheled) is the length of a life, as in 39:6.
The word (shav') is what is empty or worthless. If God does not act soon, life seems to have been given for nothing.

source.text: מִ֤י גֶ֣בֶר יִֽ֭חְיֶה וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֶה־מָּ֑וֶת יְמַלֵּ֨ט נַפְשׁ֖וֹ מִיַּד־שְׁא֣וֹל סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is the] man [who] will live and not see death, will deliver his soul from [the] hand of Sheol? Selah.

en.L: Who [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} [who] will live and not see death, [who] will deliver {{gender:their|his}} soul from the hand of Sheol? Selah
en.B: Who can go on living and never see death? Who can save their own life from the grip of Sheol? Selah
en.R: No one can live forever and never die. No one can escape from the place of the dead. Selah

decisions.reason: To see death is to experience it (16:10).

decisions.choice: the hand of Sheol: the power of death
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (6:6); its "hand" is its grip.
Readable turns the questions, which expect the answer "no one", into statements.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: אַיֵּ֤ה׀חֲסָדֶ֖יךָ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֥ים׀אֲדֹנָ֑י נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לְ֝דָוִ֗ד בֶּאֱמוּנָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [are] your former loyal loves, my Lord, [which] you swore to David in your faithfulness?

en.L: Where [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} former loyal loves, my Lord, [which] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore to David in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness?
en.B: Lord, where are the acts of loyal love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed in the past, the ones {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore to David by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness?
en.R: Lord, where is the faithful love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed in the past? You promised it to David with an oath, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful.

decisions.choice: your former loyal loves: the acts of loyal love in the past
decisions.reason: The plural takes up the first words of the psalm (verse 2). The psalm began by singing of them and now asks where they are.
As in 86:3.
As in verse 2 ('emunah).

source.text: זְכֹ֣ר אֲ֭דֹנָי חֶרְפַּ֣ת עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ שְׂאֵתִ֥י בְ֝חֵיקִ֗י כָּל־רַבִּ֥ים עַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember, my Lord, [the] reproach of your servants, my bearing in my bosom all [the] many peoples,

en.L: Remember, my Lord, the reproach of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, [how] I bear in my bosom [the reproach of] all the many peoples,
en.B: Lord, keep in mind the scorn heaped on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants; I hold within me the insults of all the many peoples,
en.R: Lord, remember how people make fun of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants. I have to carry in my heart the insults of many nations.

decisions.choice: bear in my bosom all the many peoples: carry their insults
decisions.reason: The line is very short: "my bearing in my bosom all the many peoples". The reproach of verse 51a is understood: he carries the insults that the nations heap on God's people. Some Hebrew manuscripts have "your servant", the king.

decisions.choice: in my bosom: held close, like a burden in the arms
decisions.reason: Moses speaks of carrying the people "in your bosom" like a nurse with a child (Numbers 11:12).
As in 86:3.

decisions.choice: the reproach of (L); the insults of (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the word understood from the first half (m1).
The sentence continues into verse 52, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר חֵרְפ֖וּ אוֹיְבֶ֥יךָ׀יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חֵ֝רְפ֗וּ עִקְּב֥וֹת מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: with which your enemies have taunted, YHWH, with which they have taunted [the] footsteps of your anointed.

en.L: with which {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies have taunted, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, with which they have taunted the footsteps of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed.
en.B: the insults {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies have hurled, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the taunts that have dogged every step of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed king.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies have insulted us. They have mocked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen king at every step he takes.

decisions.choice: the footsteps of your anointed: everywhere he goes
alternatives: those who come after your anointed
decisions.reason: The word ('aqev) is the heel or footprint. The enemies mock every step the king takes; some read it as mocking his successors.
Hebrews 11:26 speaks of Moses counting "the reproach of Christ" (the Anointed) greater riches than Egypt, words that may echo the Greek of verses 51-52.
As in verse 39.

source.text: בָּר֖וּךְ יְהוָ֥ה לְ֝עוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן׀וְאָמֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH forever. Amen and amen.

en.L: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever. Amen and amen.
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be blessed forever! Amen and amen.
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever and ever! Amen and amen.

decisions.reason: This blessing ends Book Three of the Psalms (Psalms 73-89), as 41:14 ends Book One and 72:18-19 ends Book Two. Book Four opens with Psalm 90. The blessing closes the whole book as well as this psalm.
The word ('amen) comes from the same root as 'emunah, "faithfulness": it means that what is said is firm and true. Doubled, it is a strong response (41:14).
To bless God is to praise him and speak well of him for what he is and does.
